## Design

### 2026-10-09 – October 9: Choosing the Parts of My Starbie, its layout, Getting the screen to work

**3h**

October 9: Choosing the Parts of My Starbie, its layout, Getting the screen to work

*First Idea and Design of the Starbie*

The first step in my project was deciding what my Starbie should do, since I didn't actually know what a Starbie was supposed to be. So here is what I came up with:
1.	Provide information about room temperature, humidity, and weather conditions if possible.
2.	Tell me the time and date and allow me to set timers.
3.	Make facial expressions like a normal pet.
4.	Interact with me through movement and voice commands.
5.	Have a notification indicator that only alerts me to important notifications.
6.	Use AI to answer basic questions. idk if possible :)

*Required Parts*

1.	Microcontroller: To support AI functionalities, the chip needs to have Wi-Fi, so my options were either ESP32 or Raspberry Pi. Although the Raspberry Pi significantly outperforms the ESP32, using an ESP32 and running the AI model on my main PC or an old PC would be a much better option in terms of both performance and budget.
2.	MPU6050 (gyroscope/accelerometer): detect Starbie's movements.
3.	DHT11/DHT22 sensor: measure temperature and humidity.
4.	RGB LED and 6 mm button: indicate different power states (system on or off).
5.	OLED SH1107: a square 128 x 128 screen.
6.	Two mechanical keyboard switches: for future features I might want to add.

*Choosing the PCB Layout*

Initially, I tried visualizing the layout using Wokwi, but I had no luck since wokwi didn't support adding a custom PCB. Anyways, I decided to save this for later, for now I just organized the components putting the screen dead center and everything else around it.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/43e408a1d473d543d510156806408c82dc2bc97b2afd142de6a3c86a87368a44.png)

*First Connections and Checkup*

I decided to stick with Wokwi and connect all the components virtually so I could understand how to wire them on the PCB. This would also give me the opportunity to program and test the basic functions of the starbie. Here is how each component is connected for now:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/e826cf224e46c0a0b933e81edba76735f8346873d3ee0ec2725dad45c6c58b4a.png)

*Testing the Connections Before Building the Main PCB*

Since I'm a noob in electronics and don't own any physical components yet, my only option was to test the basic firmware functions using Wokwi.
I decided to start by programming the screen. This was a tedious task to do on my own. I tried using AI to explain how to set it up, but that didn't go well. However, after watching this amazing video here (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=___p9JYbTc0), writing the screen code became much easier.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/b172270de58400657e595388003d1a7395c95a442602a0626bd49bb1615910ee.png)
buuuuuuuuuuut, As you can see, the screen is blank, why, I have no ided. I rewatched the video again, but everything seemed correct.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/83b745f15d77fcd8f1eb773e2d7c6a8bc6373efba6d2886c5f7c5ce4d8ff5ca6.png)
Bingoooooo! I got it working, It turned out that each screen has its own driver and requires specific libraries. After adding the correct SH110X libraries, everything worked like a charm. “ ignore the code error in the screenshot :P “

TL;DR: In this session, I am done with the Starbie's design, chose the components and their layout, set up the initial screen code, and displayed text on a screen for the very first time ever. Stay tuned for what's coming next!!!

Time spent on this session: 3 hours

### 2026-10-11 – October 10: Final Starbie and PCB Design

**3h**

October 10: Final Starbie and PCB Design

*Adding a few extra Parts to the project.*

There were a few parts I forgot to include in the previous session:
1. A vibrating motor: Makes Starbie go puuuuur. (like the motor in PlayStation controllers).
2. Buttons and LEDs: One set for each leg of Starbie.
3. Speaker: So Starbie can make a sound while it puuuuuuuuuuuurs.

*Schematic*

Instead of figuring out how to connect everything in Wokwi like last time, I decided to go straight to KiCad.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/35a38d3fb5798a242f366c45b89c5a1bf79ab6435b30bb121385ee5952ff52c6.png)

This wasn't what I expected. After a lot of suffering, I finally managed to add the Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C3 schematic. I tried to find its schemcatic on the official website, but luckily it was already included in the Hack Club care package.

Since I used the ESP32-WROOM-32 in my previous session, as it was the only version available in Wokwi, I had to figure out all the connections again.

Wellllll, I took a quick look at the market in my country and discovered that the ESP32-C3 was difficult to find. On the other hand, ESP32-WROOM-32 boards were everywhere, so I decided to return to the WROOM-32. Yaaay! This also means that I have to find a KiCad model for it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/ea20d25f17f8ee92ba4d0390f46cc8ea11df9cde60e405f70d6d325968984eba.png)

 After what felt like forever, I finally found a schematic for an ESP32 development board here: in this site:
https://forum.kicad.info/t/esp32-dev-ch340-c-symbol-and-footprint/56483/13

I managed to connect the ESP32 to the MPU6050. The next step was adding the OLED screen, but I couldn't find a model for it anywhere on the World Wide Web. So, I gave up searching. Looks like I'll have to create it myself!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/f8d79d8b31c5b728d175aee1e31842ce497786135cb5fc13033284dd9c67b3f8.png)
I just finished creating the screen's schematic and assiged it a footprint. I also finished connecting the sensors.

For now i decided to take a break from the schematic, and start working on the pcb, While watching a couple of tutorials, I decided to work on the PCB shape while at it . I searched the internet and found this gorgeous image on Pinterest!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/b7de05ec33beb8d6421fbdfc8efb01cdf749d8dcffc178107140c5dcb0496757.png)

The Starbie design created by the Hack Club team measures 90 mil × 98 mil. I feel like this is a bit large, so I decided to make mine 77 mm × 84 mm. The reason for these specific dimensions is that the Pinterest design consists of 12 × 11 LEGO pieces. I used a grid where each piece represents a 7 mm × 7 mm square.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/c09a957b1b31d08dd8a6c8d4a7035783b4343b099569144d794a00bfeb8cae83.png)

I selected the Edge.Cuts layer and started outlining. However, as shown in the picture, the edges weren't connecting correctly. I searched for a while andi feel like the problem is related to using the closed-rectangle tool instead of another tool I don't know about yet. Unfortunately, I couldn't find anything useful, so I'll call it a day for now.

TL;DR This session, I added new components to the project, finished the schematic (almost), and started working on the PCB design. There's still a long way to go!

Total Time Spent This Session: 3 hours

### 2026-10-11 – October 11: PCB Time!

**6h**

October 11: PCB Time!

*Finishing the Schematic*

I added five buttons and LEDs, one for each leg of Starbie. Each button will be assigned to a main functionality, such as weather, time, ...etc.

This was my first idea for connecting them: pressing a button would light up an LED. However, I suspected that I might have made a mistake.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/1aac63c5af698483aa6741fde4fe57c9222f97933f90bf07d4601ee548e9b556.png)

I checked the connections, and everything seemed fine, so I continued by adding a power on/off button connected to GPIO 33, since it has RTC capabilities.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/d7eccf2bbb31d27ed303ce4e65426968b7c8cd0932d922270215e047b0fa9195.png)

*Adding the Vibration Motor*

The next step is adding a vibration motor. After a quick search, I found that coin vibration motors would be suitable for the project; the motor is paired with an N-channel MOSFET since GPIO pins can't provide it with enough juice.

After finding the correct schematic, footprint, and wiring, this was the result!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/e9cb4785d2944fc79785f251fa2430b6a4e29b0fceaf1e83a198a6791d2321cf.png)

I also looked into adding a speaker, but I couldn't find anything useful for now. From what I saw, it would require an external power source, so I decided that this would be the final schematic for now.

*PCB Time Again*
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/ead448d2b9d392e4a59fe7cd32534221324d09af15640f2dcb8f0537e0898ca4.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/25734ffd2c7ac0545b62b94c6d9c253575752f913ffa2540854bb830a69054b9.png)

Updating the schematic in the PCB editor revealed a couple of errors. After some second thoughts,
none of the footprints were assigned correctly, except for the ESP32. Time to fix those!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/98a943a7628ca4a2b83b766e9dc8960a430bc9c60a71c3203700cab8411642a9.png)

This is my progress after an hour or so of editing, searching, and troubleshooting. I think now only the buttons were missing.

I was wrong. I was so, so wrong. Everything is a mess!

Out of sheer desperation, I reopened the Starbie .kicad_sch file created by the Hack Club team to find the schematics and footprints I needed.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/b8bbbf33faeece16333b489a6ddc813f0a4e885458ecc0e6ce98f3cba4c8e720.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/fa79b09283bb32294f89ecab6c9d30ed77ddb4b89311ea044abed820b8426f04.png)
Finally, I have the correct schematic and footprints!

* Getting the PCB Shape Right*

I finally managed to get the PCB outline right! It turns out that using the polygon tool instead of the rectangle tool was the solution.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/c15b9e5c0706d404a1b0b313ee01c4074fc92c7613c5b6064a4f5a342c9987e6.png)

Decided that the LEDs looked horrible, so I removed them. I'm still not sure how important it was to connect all the components in the schematic, but from what I can see, it didn't seem to make much difference to the layout itself.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/bfc249b1bfd7b04847b956527a5bab584fb93bb4e940d241abdb671a0d7b247d.png)

I also placed the ESP32 on the back of the board, while the rest of the components are on the front.

Now, only the connections remain... I guess!
